claims-acct-unlock@25.2.1 ships no source code; package.json declares a single dependency 'node-acct-utilssss21' resolved from a bare HTTPS tarball URL on an unrelated GitHub user's repository (github.com/GamerD11/ping_test) at the mutable branch ref refs/heads/main, with no commit pin and no integrity hash. On npm install, npm fetches whatever bytes are currently served at that URL and installs them as a dependency, running any lifecycle scripts bundled inside. The repository owner can replace the tarball contents at any time without any change to this package. ## Source: amazon-inspector (0d2085fa4916157b99799df085aa11e3d29bdb9a47f5798c85375b1bfdf8bd7e)
Package name `wrangler-deploy` is close to Cloudflare's official `wrangler` CLI, which raises confusion-risk concerns for developers who may install it expecting an official Cloudflare tool. Pattern-based signals fired on `dist/cli/index.js`, `dist/core/dev-ui.js`, `dist/core/runtime.js`, `dist/core/sandbox-proxy.js`, and `dist/core/crypto.js` based on co-occurrence of keywords like `ping`, `POST`/`GET`, `Buffer.from(..., 'base64')`, and `hostname` in minified/bundled code. These keyword patterns are consistent with a Wrangler-shaped CLI (HTTP requests to Cloudflare APIs, dev server, base64 token handling) but cannot be conclusively distinguished from exfiltration patterns without semantic verification of the bundled code. No specific attacker-controlled endpoint, credential-harvest path, install-time lifecycle hook, or dropper has been identified. Routing to human review to verify whether the package is a legitimate Cloudflare-adjacent tool, an unofficial deploy wrapper, or a name-confusion squat with hidden behavior in the minified bundles.

Multiple shipped bundles under dist/ (dist/index.cjs, dist/applications/index.cjs, dist/sandbox-image.cjs, dist/function-agent/main.cjs, dist/function-executor/main.cjs, and their.js counterparts) combine require("child_process") with repeated POST request primitives and shell utilities such as curl and ping, including host/id-collection patterns alongside outbound HTTP calls. Package bcxhdh1kjlopsde@1.0.0 publishes a single file, index.html, declared as the package `main`. The HTML impersonates a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, fetches an AES-CTR-encrypted value from api.keyval.org using a hardcoded lookup key (`DC7tr9PjVqMIf1EYczH1puouOG21C0khV3VzWnxdtI`), decrypts it in the browser to resolve a destination host, calls `/api/strategies/check?cid=...` on that host, and `window.location.replace`s the visitor to the returned URL. The package name is random and there is no JavaScript entry point, no lifecycle script, and no code that executes on `npm install` or `require()` — HTML is not a JS module, so a developer installing or importing this package is not harmed by its contents. The artifact appears to be a cloaked-redirect / traffic-distribution phishing page using api.keyval.org as an encrypted dead-drop for the destination host, misused as a hosting channel on the npm registry rather than a functioning Node package.

The rclone install.sh fetches from rclone's official domain, which is aggressive-but-legitimate runtime tool installation rather than a dropper. The scripts fire only when a user explicitly invokes the corresponding skill, not on `npm install`.

tailwind-kinetic (2.0.6, 2.0.8) is a Tailwind CSS plugin from the fake job interview campaign behind MAL-2026-17665 and MAL-2026-17666: the same Animate.css integration template, README and description, published by keinsell-jh on 2026-09-28. src/motion.js:5 requires the private scoped package @aaron205whitmore/postcss-animate-utils, which is not readable on the public registry and resolves only with the npm token committed in the lure repository's web/.npmrc, so the code it delivers runs when tailwind.config.js loads the plugin and the dev server starts. The published tarball contains no install scripts and no network code; the payload lives in the private dependency, which was not retrieved. Twenty-six such packages under seventeen accounts were published between 2026-07-28 and 2026-10-09.
